importance_ranking.reason: Significant visual variation between structure types (PEB portal frame, steel truss, tensile membrane, open-sided vs fully enclosed). Buyers use the image to confirm this is a badminton court shed — not a generic industrial or warehouse shed — before reading any text. Wrong structure type or wrong application context = immediate skip.

Clear height (BWF minimum 9 m), court count, structure type, and service scope are non-negotiable technical gates. A listing without these specs cannot be evaluated for fit — buyers shortlist and eliminate entirely based on spec match before any other signal.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant shed fabricator brand with buyer recall exists in this category; buyers search by spec, location, and past project references — not by fabricator brand name. JSW Steel appears in buyer vocabulary for roofing sheet material but is a raw material brand, not a shed fabricator brand.
importance_ranking.reason: This is a high-value capital construction project. Buyers evaluate fabricator credentials, IS 800 compliance capability, past sports facility project references, and ability to provide engineering drawings during vendor selection — seller identity is a meaningful qualification signal after spec shortlisting.

Price varies substantially with court count, structure type, roofing material, and service scope (supply-only vs turnkey). Indian buyers compare per-sq-ft rates aggressively but only after confirming spec and scope equivalence — raw price comparison without spec context is unreliable and misleading.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Some sellers quote per project lump sum for turnkey contracts — creates price comparison confusion. Per sq ft of covered area is the dominant and standard comparison unit; must be shown alongside price to enable meaningful cross-listing comparison.
importance_ranking.reason: Per sq ft vs per project lump sum is a real market ambiguity in this category. Price cannot be compared across listings without knowing the unit basis — a lump-sum quote and a per-sq-ft quote for the same project scope are not directly comparable without unit clarity.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Defines the scale of the entire structure — single vs double vs multi-court configurations are non-interchangeable and represent the largest price delta of any spec, as footprint, structural span, and material quantity change entirely with court count.

PEB, steel truss, tensile, and tubular truss are fundamentally different engineering systems with non-interchangeable cost profiles, lead times, and structural capabilities — PEB commands a significant premium over tubular truss for equivalent footprint.

missing_important_specs.why_important: IS 875 wind zone compliance is a structural design input that buyers in coastal and high-wind regions (Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat) explicitly specify — sellers need this to confirm their standard design meets the structural safety requirement for the project location.

The internal column-free span width determines whether the structure can cover the required court width without obstructing play — critical for multi-court layouts where internal columns would be a disqualifying defect.

Thermal insulation treatment (sandwich panel, air-bubble foil, or none) is a distinct buyer requirement from roofing sheet material — it affects indoor comfort for players and represents a significant cost addition that buyers specify separately from the roofing sheet choice.

top_rfq_specs.reason: BWF minimum clear height of 9 m (~30 ft) is a non-negotiable structural parameter — sellers need this to confirm their standard design meets the requirement and to size the structural frame correctly for the project.
Sellers with only PEB fabrication capability cannot supply a tensile or dome structure — this spec routes the RFQ to sellers who can actually deliver the structural system the buyer wants.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Court count is the most fundamental project-sizing parameter — it determines total footprint, structural span, and overall project cost, and sellers need it to provide any meaningful quote or confirm supply capability.

Sellers who supply prefabricated material only cannot serve a buyer needing full turnkey erection — this spec routes the RFQ to sellers with the right service capability and prevents mismatched responses.
